text.p: Russia will redenominate its inflated rouble at the beginning of next year, introducing a new rouble worth 1,000 old ones, President Boris Yeltsin said on Monday.
Ordinary people would not lose from the reform, which was possible because inflation of basic goods had mostly been eliminated, Yeltsin said in a statement.

"Nobody will lose anything as a result of this reform," Yeltsin said, referring to repeated currency reforms under the Soviet regime which wiped out ordinary people's savings. Yeltsin said people would not be forced to swap their banknotes for new ones. Current banknotes would remain valid until the end of 1998, and people would be able to exchange them at central bank offices until the end of 2002.
Yeltsin said people knew that the excessive price rises which pushed annual inflation in 1993 into four digits was no more.

"The prices of basic goods are practically stable and we are determined and certain that they will remain so. That is why we took this decision to carry out a monetary reform. And with it we declare today: There will be no more inflation," he said.

Yeltsin said the rouble had become one of Eastern Europe's most stable currencies and people being paid in roubles no longer had to rush to exchange it for dollars. They could keep their savings in rouble accounts. "People must know for sure that we will not try to solve the country's economic problems with the help of the printing press," he added.
